purpose: Read-only research and creative dossier for the Sepulchre60 ECC/CDC workshop redesign. Proposed programme, titles and design directions are recommendations, not announced event facts.

scope.method: Broad review of the official publications index (1992 onward), talks index (2012-2026) and editorial index (2020-2024); selected paper abstracts, introductions and substantive sections; complete two-page editorials and substantial sections of the 2018 ECC/CDC slide decks. This is not a claim to have fully read every publication or watched all talks.
scope.arc: An enduring question is how feedback gives a system a useful form of behaviour. Constructive nonlinear design supplies the foundation; geometry shapes algorithms and collective motion; differential methods recover tractable structure; mixed feedback explains sensitivity, switching and rhythmic adaptation across scales. Recent spiking work connects these strands rather than replacing them.

recommendation.ecc_subtitle: Ideas carried forward — an alumni gathering
recommendation.cdc_subtitle: Connections across control — friends and collaborators
recommendation.rationale: Forms accommodates geometry, constructed dynamics, rhythmic patterns and musical form. Feedback names the intellectual through-line. It is broad enough for both gatherings, while the subtitles distinguish transmission across generations from exchange across fields.
recommendation.central_question: How does interaction give rise to form, rhythm and adaptation?
recommendation.draft_intro: A conversation across nonlinear control, geometry, collective behaviour and biological rhythms. Two gatherings bring together the people and ideas connected by Rodolphe Sepulchre’s work: the questions we share, the paths they have opened, and what comes next.
recommendation.music_grounding: The connection to music is explicit in Sepulchre’s Clocks and Rhythms editorial: rhythmic systems are open to their environment, and musical experience depends on modulation between notes. Use this as a thread about responsiveness and listening, rather than treating music as decorative imagery.
recommendation.cultural_grounding: The love of music, Belgian identity and French intellectual ideals were supplied by the user. Treat these as design inspiration, not as newly established biographical claims. Express them through measured prose, thoughtful conversation, conviviality and a small amount of French where meaningful; avoid invented philosophical allegiances, attributed quotations or national stereotypes.
recommendation.visual_direction: An essay or chamber-music programme: warm paper, dark ink, one restrained wine-red accent, a strong serif title, generous silence around text, and a small official portrait. A sparse abstract line motif can suggest trajectories, phase and counterpoint. Research topics must retain equal visibility; avoid letting neuron imagery imply that the whole career is exclusively neuroscience.
recommendation.interaction_direction: An optional slow motif of distinct paths becoming coordinated can express interaction without forced unison. Keep it clearly abstract, provide a static reduced-motion state, and let programme and readings remain immediately usable.

programme.status: Illustrative one-day structure; proposed topics and roles only. Eight research slots total, each 25 minutes plus 5 minutes of questions. Do not infer speaker invitations, acceptances or event logistics.

programme.ecc_treatment: Let alumni lead the eight research slots. Ask each to connect one question developed with Rodolphe to a direction they now pursue. Pair chairs across generations. Keep personal recollections in the dedicated tribute time, leaving room for substantial science.
programme.cdc_treatment: Let collaborators illuminate connections among the same broad themes. Ask each for one shared intellectual turning point and one unresolved question. Pair adjacent talks from different fields and invite the audience into the panel.
programme.music: If organisers want live music, a brief contribution at the reception or immediately after the formal close gives it a clear place without reducing research discussion. This is a format suggestion, not a claim that any performer or programme is arranged.

date_corrections: Cellular switches orchestrate rhythmic circuits: online 3 September 2018; Biological Cybernetics volume 113, pages 71-82, is 2019. Label 2019, optionally adding online 2018.

Control Across Scales by Positive and Negative Feedback: review first online 10 December 2018, volume publication May 2019. The CDC lecture is December 2018. Keep lecture and publication dates distinct.
Spiking Control Systems: 2021 arXiv submission, March 2022 revision, May 2022 journal publication.

Differential dissipativity theory for dominance analysis: 2017 preprint, 2018 revision, June 2019 journal publication. Do not use the automatically generated 2026 date displayed in experimental arXiv HTML as publication date.
Constructive Nonlinear Control: original copyright/publication year 1997; later electronic and softcover dates are editions, not the research's beginning.
Optimization Algorithms on Matrix Manifolds: 2008 in the authors' official bibliography.
